t: The OpenCanvas logos, and how to name OpenCanvas in a product that embeds it. Credit is welcome and never required.

Use the files as they are: don't recolour, stretch, crop or add effects. Leave clear space of at least a quarter of the logo's height around it. Mark and wordmark, light backgrounds Download the light-background logo, SVG Mark and wordmark, dark backgrounds Download the dark-background logo, SVG Mark alone, for small spaces (at least 16 px) Download the mark, SVG

Preferred: Powered by OpenCanvas Alternative: Built with OpenCanvas Link: https://github.com/CasualOffice/opencanvas Write "OpenCanvas" as one word with a capital C. Describe it as source-available. Avoid wording that suggests a partnership or endorsement unless the project has agreed to it in writing, and don't use the OpenCanvas name or logo as your product's own.

If OpenCanvas helps you, please say so: in an application footer, an About dialog, your documentation or your third-party notices. This is a request, not a condition. OpenCanvas never adds attribution to your application or to the files it saves.

A logo used as attribution needs a text alternative: alt="Powered by OpenCanvas" on the image, or visible text beside a decorative image with alt="" . Use the light-background logo on light surfaces and the dark-background logo on dark ones, so the wordmark keeps its contrast.

Client applies change locally (instant), produces a Yjs update. Sends sync:update over WS. Room engine: role check (edit role; comment role may only touch the comments subtree) → apply to server Doc → append to room_updates (durable tail) → fan out to all peers (local + other nodes via bus if viewers are spread). Awareness (cursor, selection, pointer, colour, name) is ephemeral — never stored, fan-out only, throttled to 20 Hz.

Triggers: manual "Save version", autosave interval (default 60 s with changes), idle (30 s without edits), last user leaves, session close API, graceful shutdown. room-engine ──(dirty since last commit)──▶ commit-engine serialize Doc → .ocanvas (zip: document.json, ydoc.bin, manifest.json) POST host save callback (If-Match: last host version) 200 → record host_version, clear dirty, emit "saved" to clients 409 → host changed file outside session → emit "conflict" → policy: (a) save-as-copy callback, or (b) reload host version and merge as a new branch, per host config 5xx/timeout → outbox retry

GET /preview?token=… → server fetches file (or uses live room state if live=1 and room exists), renders static HTML via render . No WS, no Yjs on the client — fast and cacheable by (file_id, host_version) . GET /export/{format}?token=… → same source, renders MD/HTML/PDF/DOCX/PNG. After final commit succeeds and no clients remain for ROOM_TTL_SECS (default 10 min): drop room from memory, delete room_updates and snapshot rows. Nothing about the document remains on our side (Principle 3).

SQLite + in-process rooms. Handles thousands of connections. Zero dependencies.

┌───────── L7 load balancer ─────────┐ │ HTTP: round-robin │ │ WS: hash(room_id) → node (sticky) │ └───────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────┘ node-1 node-2 node-3 (identical binaries) │ owns rooms by lease │ └──── Redis (leases) ─ internal WS relay ┘ └──── MySQL/MariaDB (snapshots, tails, outbox) ────┘ One owner per room (ADR-006). The owner holds the authoritative Yrs Doc in memory. Ownership is a Redis lease ( SET room:{id}:owner node NX PX ) renewed every 5 s. If the LB routes a client to a non-owner, that node relays the connection to the owner over one internal WebSocket per client connection

Yrs apply + broadcast ≈ 10–50 µs per small update; 300 rooms × 10 upd/s = 3 000 upd/s ≪ capacity. Bottleneck is fan-out bytes, not merge. Memory: ~ 3× doc size per live room; 300 rooms × 1 MB × 3 ≈ 900 MB worst, typical 100–200 MB.

Per-host keys; JWT aud , iss , exp ≤ 10 h , jti replay cache. Role enforced server-side per frame ; client UI is advisory only. Embeds rendered in sandbox iframes from an allow-list; user HTML never rendered unsanitised; CSP frame-ancestors = host origins. Unfurl fetcher: DNS-pinned, private-IP block, size/time caps. No document content in logs; PII limited to display name/avatar in memory.

Docker image (distroless, ~20 MB) + docker-compose.yml (single node, SQLite) + docker-compose.cluster.yml (3 nodes, MariaDB, Redis, nginx). Helm chart (P2). Config via env vars + optional opencanvas.toml . Graceful shutdown: stop accepting, commit all dirty rooms, release leases.

h: 7. Findings for the server (not fixed here)
t: Memory per idle connection is high (0.20 MB). Not root-caused. A likely part is the WebSocket read buffer, which tungstenite allocates per connection (128 KiB by default) and which collab::upgrade does not set. Checking needs a heap profile; a smaller read_buffer_size on the WebSocketUpgrade would be the first thing to try. Room memory is 5–14× the document , not the "~3× doc size" in docs/03 §5.3; docs/03's 300-room estimate is low for database/board-heavy documents. ** /metrics lists fewer series than docs/13 says.** The server exports oc_rooms_active , oc_connections_active , oc_launches_to

t: Situation Result Two users type in the same paragraph Both texts kept, interleaved by position (Yjs YATA). No lost characters. Both bold overlapping ranges Union of marks. One bolds, other unbolds same range → last writer per character. One deletes a block while another types in it Delete wins; the typing is lost and the typer is notified ("Block removed by Asha · Undo"). Their undo restores it. Both move the same block Last move wins (single final position, never duplicated). Table: one adds a column, other adds a row Both applied; new cells empty. Each connection publishes a small state (≤ 2 KB, ≤ 20 Hz): { "user": { "id": "u_123", "name": "Asha Rao", "color": "#7c3aed", "avatar": "…", "role": "edit" }, "cursor": { "anchor": <RelativePosition>, "head": <RelativePosition> }, "board": { "id": "brd_1", "x": 412.5, "y": 80, "tool": "pen", "selection": ["s_9"] }, "view": { "blockId": "b_44" }, // what they are looking at, for "follow" "typing": true, "idle": false } user fields are overwritten by the server from the session grant — clients cannot spoof names/colours. Cursor positions are Yjs relative positions , so they stay correct while te

Text: caret = 2 px bar in user colour + name label (shown on move, fades after 2 s idle, shown on hover). Selection = 20 % tint of user colour. Labels collision-avoid (stack upward) when carets are on the same line. Board: pointer arrow + name tag in user colour, interpolated (60 fps lerp) between 20 Hz updates; selection outline in user colour; "laser" tool leaves a fading trail. Off-screen collaborators: avatar stack in the top bar. h: Can I use it in production today?
t: Not yet. OpenCanvas is a P1 alpha for evaluation. The server, the editor, the database and whiteboard blocks and the sample host run end to end, and most work is built and verified, but it still awaits the owner's review and there is no tagged release. The roadmap shows each item's status.

Only while a session is live. The server keeps a snapshot and the recent updates so it survives a restart and late joiners can catch up, and deletes them after the session is saved and idle. The file lives in your app; OpenCanvas writes it back there. See Architecture .

To your app, not to OpenCanvas. Your backend checks access and signs a short-lived launch token naming the file, the user and the role (view, comment or edit). OpenCanvas trusts that decision for the life of the token, enforces it on every edit, and switches a user's role live when your app calls the role API. See the integration guide .

No. Every change saves to your app on a short timer, when the canvas goes idle, when the last person leaves and when the server shuts down. Saves go through a durable outbox, so a restart resends them. If your copy of the file changed elsewhere, your chosen policy runs: save a copy, or reload.

h: We already use Collabora through WOPI. Can we reuse that?
t: Yes. OpenCanvas is a WOPI client: discovery, CheckFileInfo, GetFile, PutFile and PUT_RELATIVE, with an allow-list for the WOPISrc URLs it will call. Proof keys are not supported yet. See WOPI mode .

h: What can it import and export?
t: Export: Markdown, HTML, JSON, the native .ocanvas file, Word, and PDF when the operator runs the optional Gotenberg sidecar (otherwise the editor prints to PDF). Whiteboards export as SVG and PNG. Import: Markdown, HTML and CSV. See Operations .

One node runs on SQLite. For more users, run several nodes against MySQL or MariaDB with Redis: each room has one owner node, other nodes relay to it, and if the owner dies another node takes the room over from its log. See Operations and Architecture .

h: Does the demo send anything anywhere?
t: No. The demo is the real editor running against a document in your browser, with simulated collaborators. There is no server behind it, and exports that need a server say so.

The server, the editor and the sample host on your machine, from the project's README. To look around first, open the demo : it runs in your browser with no server. Status: P1 alpha. The server, editor, database and whiteboard blocks, and the sample host all run end to end. See the tracker for what is done and what is open.

Your app ── signs launch token (who, which file, which role) ──▶ OpenCanvas iframe ◀── load / save / assets / users / copies callbacks ── OpenCanvas server You own authentication, users, ACL, files, versions and retention. OpenCanvas owns the editor, real-time merge (Yjs CRDT), presence and cursors, preview, export, and autosave back to your storage. OpenCanvas keeps nothing once a session is saved and idle. Its database only holds the transient room log and the save outbox.

Status: draft v0.1, 2026-11-21. This is the contract an integrating application implements. Modelled on Collabora Online's WOPI integration ( 01 §4 ). Golden rule: your application decides who may open which file with what role. OpenCanvas trusts that decision for the life of the token and enforces it on every edit. Your application stores the file.

Every call carries Authorization: Bearer <callbackToken> and X-OpenCanvas-Signature: t=<ts>,v1=<hex>,v2=<hex> so you can verify the call comes from OpenCanvas: v2 = hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<ts>.<METHOD>.<path?query>.<body>" ). Verify this one. It binds the request method and path, so a captured signature can't be replayed against another endpoint. v1 = hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<ts>.<body>" ), kept for hosts written before v2. Reject timestamps more than 5 minutes off, and compare in constant time. OpenCanvas never follows redirects from your callbacks: answer directly. e

Revoke or downgrade a user live when you change ACLs: POST /v1/files/{fileId}/role {"userId":"u_123","role":"view"} — the user's open session switches to read-only immediately (or is closed with "role":"none" ). Roles: view | comment | edit | none . Answers 200 {"connections":1,"sessions":2} (live connections switched, tickets updated); 401 API_KEY_INVALID for a wrong host/key, 400 ROLE_INVALID . Patch content from a bot: POST /v1/files/{fileId}/patch (see 04 §6) with {"ops":[…],"author":{"id","name"}} . Ops: append , insertAfter

One live room per (host, file). Users who open the same file join the same room — there is no fork. The room loads your file once. Your file is updated by commits only. Autosave commits are flagged X-OpenCanvas-Autosave: 1 so you can collapse them in version history. At-least-once commit with idempotency key; final commit before room close; on graceful shutdown all dirty rooms commit. Nothing is retained after the room closes and TTL passes. Role changes you make during a session take effect only when you call the role API or the token expires — tokens are the contract.

Product: OpenCanvas — an embeddable, real-time collaborative canvas (rich document + board) built for integration . Status: draft v0.1, 2026-11-21. Awaiting approval. Owner: schnsrw1@gmail.com

Every product that wants a "Slack/Zoom/Loop-style canvas" today has two bad options: build a collaborative editor from scratch (months of CRDT, cursor, conflict and export work) or adopt a SaaS whose storage, users and permissions are not theirs. Collabora Online solved this for office files: the host keeps files, users and ACLs, the editor does editing. Nobody offers that model for a modern block canvas.

Drop one iframe (or one web component) into any app and its users get a live, multi-cursor canvas — text, tables, images, links, embeds and boards — while the app keeps full ownership of the file, the users and who can do what.

Host owns identity, ACL and storage. OpenCanvas never authenticates users, never decides permissions, never keeps the canonical file. We own editing. Real-time merge, presence, cursors, preview, export, commit back to host. No document persistence beyond a live session. Session state (CRDT snapshot + update tail) is kept only to survive node restarts and to let late joiners catch up; it is deleted after commit + idle TTL. Lightweight. One server binary; SQLite by default; one JS bundle. Runs on a 1 vCPU / 512 MB box for a small team. Scalable. Stateless HTTP, room-affine WebSocket nodes, MySQL

User accounts, login, sharing dialogs, folder trees (host's job). Long-term storage, retention, backup of documents (host's job). AI features (P3, pluggable provider). Spreadsheets / slides as blocks (link to OpenCalc / OpenSlide via embed). Native mobile apps (responsive web only).

No manual save anywhere (ADR-012). A room saves when it is dirty and: 2 s have passed since the last update ( OC_AUTOSAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS ), or 10 s have passed since the first unsaved update ( OC_AUTOSAVE_MAX_MS ), or the last client leaves, or the process gets SIGTERM. Saves are serialized per room. Each commit ( .ocanvas bytes, idempotency key, base version, sealed callback token) is written to commit_outbox as pending before the PUT; retries resend the same row. 200 marks it done (payload dropped), 409 conflict , a newer commit marks older pending rows superseded . A failure is retried with ba

OC_KEK (base64 of 32 bytes) seals the host callback token (in WOPI mode: the access token) in sessions.grant_json and commit_outbox.token with AES-256-GCM ( enc:v1:<base64(nonce‖ct)> , bound to the row id). The server refuses to start without it unless OC_DEV=1 (then tokens are stored in clear, with a warning). OC_MAX_DOC_MB (20) caps the encoded document; 60 frames/s (burst 120) per socket. p: OpenCanvas: a collaborative canvas you embed
h: A live canvas inside your app. Your files stay yours.
t: OpenCanvas is a collaborative canvas you embed, the way apps embed Collabora: rich text, databases and whiteboards, with live cursors. Your application keeps the users, the permissions and the file. OpenCanvas does the editing, merges every change live, and saves the file back to you on its own. Try the demo Run it with Docker The demo is the real editor running in your browser on a sample canvas, with simulated collaborators: no server, no account, nothing sent. Pre-release: read the limits first. Source-available (BUSL-1.1), free to self-host and embed One Rust server Your app keeps the file

p: OpenCanvas: a collaborative canvas you embed
t: Your backend checks who may open which file, signs a short launch token, and opens OpenCanvas in an iframe. From then on OpenCanvas runs the live session and calls your app back to load and save the file. Once a session is saved and idle, it keeps nothing. Your app owns Sign-in, users, who can view, comment or edit, the file itself, its versions and its retention. OpenCanvas owns The editor, real-time merge, cursors and presence, preview, export, and autosave back to your storage. One server A Rust binary with the editor built in. SQLite by default; MySQL or MariaDB and Redis when you run seve

p: OpenCanvas: a collaborative canvas you embed
t: Every change is a small update that merges with everyone else's in any order, the same way on every screen. The server orders and relays updates; it never has to resolve a conflict between two people typing. So: live co-editing without locks, and brief disconnects resync on their own. Host callbacks

p: OpenCanvas: a collaborative canvas you embed
t: OpenCanvas loads the file from your app when a session opens and writes it back with a plain HTTP call, signed so you know it is us. If your file changed elsewhere, your chosen policy runs: save a copy, or reload. So: your storage, versions and retention rules stay the only ones. Autosave

p: OpenCanvas: a collaborative canvas you embed
t: Changes save on a short timer, when the canvas goes idle, when the last person leaves and when the server shuts down. Each save is written to an outbox first, so a restart resends it rather than losing it. So: the status reads Saved, and that is true.

p: OpenCanvas: a collaborative canvas you embed
h: One container to start, more nodes when you need them.
t: A single node runs on SQLite with no database to set up. For many concurrent users, point several nodes at MySQL or MariaDB and Redis: each room has one owner node, and the others relay to it. Single node, SQLite docker run -p 8080:8080 -v oc-data:/data \ -e OC_PUBLIC_URL=https://canvas.example.com \ -e OC_KEK=$(openssl rand -base64 32) \ -e OC_HOSTS_FILE=/data/opencanvas.hosts.toml \ opencanvas/server:0.1 Cluster DATABASE_URL=mysql://oc:***@mariadb:3306/opencanvas REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379 # enables cluster mode OC_NODE_ID=node-1 OC_CLUSTER_ADVERTISE=http://node-1:8080 OC_CLUSTER_SECRET=<s
